coupled decisions: the outcome is tied to the separate inline-script proposal #995

competing implementations: PRs #245, #356 and #406 each embodied a different answer

votes as evidence: 83 reactions on the opener and many +1 use cases signalled demand without a structured tally

votes as evidence: hundreds of reactions and repeated me-too comments were the main pressure but were never weighed explicitly
votes as evidence: the designer's external straw poll results were never reported back, so the tally behind option 2 is invisible
decider not in thread: the designer deferred to an MVP design the maintainer had made before joining, which is not in the issue

decider not in thread: the team that blocked #14520 never stated its threat model in the issue despite a user asking
decider not in thread: a reviewer approved but waited on the lead maintainer, who appeared only at review checkpoints
implementation elsewhere: the deciding work happened in a separate PR thread
decision moved to another thread: the final design was argued in PR #2483 review, not the issue
decision moved to another thread: further work continues in a new Stage 2 issue
thread handoff: settling moved the conversation to a new issue rather than recording an answer here
unresolved dissent at settlement: the issue closed on merge while a collaborator's objection stood unanswered
decided too fast: closure came within a day, before key stakeholders could weigh in
contested settled decision: users kept challenging a closed decision for years with no formal reopen path
silence as consent: acceptance rested on a week passing with no objections rather than an explicit check of affected users
split scope: settling one part (strings) spun the remainder (backticks) into a new issue
living decision list: the issue served as a running list of removals, each settled in a separate PR, rather than one decision
coupled decisions: the umbrella question bundled several staged sub-decisions (no-check default, isolatedModules, emit via swc) each settled in other issues
staged acceptance: several reviewer points were explicitly deferred to follow-up PRs with no tracked record
reversal after merge: the brace choice was flipped in-thread after the implementing PR landed but before release
reversal after closing: a won't-do decision was reopened years later when a concrete design appeared
reversal after decision: settled as no, reopened with a plan and help wanted, then closed again three years later without a build
reversal after shipping: the first merged fix was changed and reverted in commits with no record in the thread until a contributor noticed
long dormancy: the question sat for three years between feasibility findings and the fix
years-long dormancy: a nine-year-old question with stalled community PRs and no record of why it waited
long dormancy: five years between framing and decision, with the maintainer's capacity as the real blocker
stalled question: a maintainer gave an early lean and then went silent for ten months, with no owner or next step recorded
prototype-first framing: the maintainer had already built it, so yes/no was settled by demonstration rather than a question
staged acceptance: the palette was agreed in December but implementation drifted across contributors and PRs for months, and the closure never links the decision to the code that shipped it
reviewer implements the answer: the maintainer settled the API by pushing commits to the contributor's branch rather than recording a choice
decisions as code suggestions: many design choices were made via suggestion blocks, so the record lives in diffs, not prose
staged acceptance: context-aware display was deferred pending an architecture refactor
external dependency: the decision waited on a separate community project being ready
coupled decisions: the answer depended on a separate multi-scene issue that was never resolved here
settled but not shipped: approved yet held for a release string freeze, so settled and merged diverge
reframing: the question shifted from 'add telemetry' to 'add a generic event hook', which needs the question itself to be renamed rather than answered
reframed question: the final answer (improve the incumbent) was not one of the options in the original framing
problem before solution: the team conceded the problem statement was never agreed, so a question about whether to solve anything was hidden inside a question about one design
reframing: many replies argued the real problem was a different menu, which the design cannot split off
follow-up defect: a missed integration (key bindings) surfaced after the decision and needed its own PR
staged acceptance: deprecation of the old tools was agreed but not yet carried out
spun-off follow-up: migration and old-integration retirement were deferred to separate issues
cross-repo build: one decision fanned out to core, frontend, brands and two docs PRs
reversal after shipping: post-ship evidence (unmaintained upstream, large-file failures) reopens the library choice without a formal revisit
stale facts: no prompt to re-verify a 'True' check when upstream changes later
stale rationale: the stated condition for revisiting depended on external Node behaviour that later changed, with nothing prompting the decider to re-check
conditional acceptance: the yes depended on the contributor committing to future maintenance, a people commitment the record cannot capture
external dependency evidence: Windows Terminal and tmux fixes upstream shaped what was viable
external alternative as answer: the outcome leans on a third-party tool (delta) endorsed in the README rather than a built feature
decider not in thread: the real deciders are Debian and Bacula maintainers, and bat's own maintainers spoke only once
external expert input: a Jupyter maintainer from outside the project steered the design, a role the design does not distinguish
per-member approvals: each TSC member's sign-off is a separate reply that the record should tally
votes as evidence: steering committee members approve with one-line replies counted as a gate
formal sign-off mechanics: rfcbot checkboxes and concerns act as the settle step, which Chopin's single settler does not model
multiple approvers per platform: GTK and macOS maintainers each signed off on their area
reversal after shipping: two implementation PRs were opened and abandoned before the final design, with the reason recorded only on a closed PR
silent option removal: an option added in response to feedback was later dropped by editing the proposal, with no recorded reasoning
reopening a decision scattered across PRs: the prior refusal lived in five closed PRs rather than one record
rejected options content: A late option with no recorded reason for non-adoption: an option whose fate has no rationale.
decider not in thread: the team had no written design philosophy, so the author built a dialog that reviewers then rejected
standing policy as decider: the outcome follows a project-wide option philosophy document rather than this thread's arguments, and the record needs to cite it
principle constraint: a standing no-options policy ruled out a popular answer, which needs to sit beside the question as a fixed constraint

convention scope: One decision with three scopes (Node.js code, frontend, isomorphic packages), only one of which changed. The choice table holds a single answer, not per-context answers where one cel
votes or reaction counts as evidence: charter seconding was counted from thumbs-up reactions, and the decision itself was a ranked Condorcet ballot
votes as evidence: the decision was a formal ranked ballot by a closed electorate with private ballots and turnout tracking, not thumbs from whoever passes by
votes as evidence: the default was settled by a quick poll of reply votes from the implementer

formal vote: A poll feeding a decision, tied 3-3, followed by a rule to let each member pick. The design has Ask and Takes (Agrees/Objects/Unsure) but no poll tally, no quorum, and no 'decide not to d
deferred question never reopened: later requests for name derivation pile up in the same thread without reviving the deferred item
limbo state: neither accepted nor rejected, only signalled by label changes
staged acceptance: a 'not at this time' deferral has no trigger or review date for reopening
deferred to a larger initiative: maintainers parked it for a future library-mode review that is not linked or tracked
residual limits after settling: tmux and lazygit cases stayed unsolved after closing
scope guarding after close: follow-on option requests were refused in the closed thread, a sub-decision the record would miss
coupled decisions: scripts and styles were treated as one question, then split when the maintainer judged styles differently
per-item settlement: the answer was a list of about seventy rules each with its own keep-or-drop call
experiments as evidence: the outcome so far is an opt-in experimental flag announced on a blog, not a settled answer

provisional decision: Reversal trigger is an environmental change (minimum platform version raised), not a new argument. The record has 'What we knew at the time' but nothing like 'revisit when X chan

provisional decision: Evidence is a dated snapshot ('at time of writing' namespace counts, comparison against Kubernetes large-cluster limits). 'What we knew' could hold it, but nothing flags it for r
provisional decision: Both ADRs say they can be revisited, but neither names a review date or trigger. The design has no 'revisit when' condition on a settled question.
screenshots as evidence: layout choices were argued with terminal screenshots, not a structured comparison
visual evidence: options were judged from rendered samples and a live preview site rather than text
visual alternatives as evidence: competing renderings were compared through screenshots
visual references as evidence: options arrived as screenshots of other tools, with no way to compare them side by side
thread moderation: locking and unlocking to steer scope has no equivalent
duplicates merged: repeated objections were hidden as duplicates rather than linked to the settled record
existing-capability check: a hidden existing action partly answered the request, a fact that needed checking before building
partial solution as closure: a different feature that met part of the need was used to close the request

moot question: Deprecated with no successor: the decision was withdrawn rather than replaced, and the repo does not say what is now true. Settled and Reopen exist, but there is no 'retired, no replace
moot question: A negative decision: the outcome removes a feature and closes a line of work. Settle writes an answer sentence into the plan, and nothing records withdrawn, dropped or not doing it.
deadline: Implementation and a Test262 PR were already waiting, so the decision carried shipping urgency that the design cannot express.
deadline: The thread ended because patience ran out and a delegate called time; there is no discussion-has-run-its-course affordance or deadline on a question.
deadline: Feedback that arrived days before a meeting changed the design and the champion said it should have come earlier; the design has no early-input nudge or feedback deadline.
consultation skipped: the maintainer asked for opinions and shipped the PR before anyone could reply
decided before discussed: the proposal named its decision and PRs were open before feedback arrived

ranked choice: A formal ranked vote among full competing documents (Condorcet over seven candidates plus a 'none yet' sentinel), run by an outside trusted party. The nearest primitive is a stance pill
ranked choice: Ordering of items is a decision type: neither a single choice nor a tune dial. There is no ranked-list shape.
